t030: "An Extended Look": Rockstar shows GTA VI gameplay today, on Netflix first
t033: exclusively for Netflix subscribers, and arrives free on Rockstar's YouTube channel and the official site at
t035: . It's a first-of-its-kind partnership between Rockstar and a streaming service — and, according to Netflix, the footage was captured entirely from the game running on PlayStation 5. Press estimates put it somewhere between 20 and 30 minutes. Right after the special, impressions from outlets and creators invited to Rockstar North go live as well.
t037: Rockstar breaks its silence on the leaks
t038: After a week of gameplay videos circulating online, the studio published an open letter saying it was heartbreaking for the team to see the material leak that way, and that this was not how it meant to show the game. The tone was personal rather than legal: Rockstar apologized for the long wait for news, thanked the community for its support and said GTA VI is "almost there".
t040: Take-Two goes to court to trace the source of the leak
t041: The publisher obtained court authorization in the United States to request data from Microsoft and Discord about accounts and communities tied to distributing the files. Microsoft said it is cooperating. Our rule at VICEVERSA is simple: we report that the leak exists, without showing or pointing to the material.
t043: Nothing has changed: launch still set for November 19
t044: Despite last week's turbulence, no new delay was announced. GTA VI remains scheduled for November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with pre-loading from November 12. The PC version still has no date.
t046: $79.99 or $99.99: what changes between the editions
t047: The standard edition costs $79.99 and the Ultimate $99.99 on the PlayStation and Xbox stores. Digital pre-orders include the Vintage Vice City Pack — vehicle, garage, clothing and an exclusive weapon finish — plus a month of GTA+ for eligible buyers. Physical boxes ship without a disc, containing only a download code.
t049: Trailer 2 pulled 475 million views in 24 hours
t050: To put today in perspective: the previous premiere, in May 2025, was described by Take-Two as the biggest video debut in history. The Extended Look is the last major official presentation before launch — and the first time Rockstar controls the narrative since the leaks.
t055: After years of rumors, the studio officially announces that the next Grand Theft Auto is in development. The internet was never the same.
t058: Dozens of videos from unfinished builds hit the web, in what journalists described as one of the largest leaks in video game history.
t060: Trailer 1 — and the return to Vice City
t061: The first trailer reveals Lucia, the state of Leonida and the return to Vice City. Published hours ahead of schedule after leaking on social media, it broke viewership records on day one.
t064: The release moves from 2025 to May 26, 2026. Four days later, the second trailer properly introduces the Jason and Lucia duo — and calms fans down (a little).
t067: Rockstar moves the release to November 19, 2026, saying it needs the extra months to deliver the level of polish the community expects.
t070: Prices announced, pre-orders live, editions detailed: $79.99 and $99.99.
t072: Rockstar and Netflix announce the Extended Look
t073: A first-of-its-kind partnership: the presentation would premiere on streaming six hours before reaching YouTube. No game had ever used a streaming platform as its primary marketing channel.
t075: The wave of leaks — and Rockstar's letter
t076: Gameplay videos start circulating almost daily from August 18. Take-Two secures court authorization to trace the source, and on the 26th Rockstar publishes an open letter regretting the episode and confirming the schedule still stands.
t079: 26 minutes of gameplay captured on a base PlayStation 5, premiering on Netflix and going free on YouTube six hours later. Reworked combat, Red Dead 2-style NPC interaction, the sixth wanted star and instant switching between the protagonists.

t134: How do I watch the Extended Look?
t135: It's already live on Netflix for subscribers, and at 9 PM ET today it becomes free on Rockstar's YouTube channel and the official GTA VI site. It runs 26 minutes. You don't need a pre-order or a Rockstar account to watch the public version.
t136: What was revealed in the Extended Look?
t137: Real gameplay captured on a base PS5 with Jason and Lucia: reworked combat, Red Dead 2-style NPC interaction, slim jim car theft, the return of the sixth wanted star, instant character switching when the pair are together, hints of a morality system and a long list of side activities — from scuba diving to dirt biking.
t138: When does GTA VI come out?
t139: On November 19, 2026, worldwide, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with pre-loading from November 12.
t140: Is it coming to PC, PS4 or Xbox One?
t141: PS4 and Xbox One will not get the game. The PC version has not been announced for launch; based on Rockstar's track record, it usually arrives 12 to 24 months after the consoles.
t143: $79.99 for the standard edition and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition, which includes the Vintage Vice City Pack and extra in-campaign perks. Pre-orders are already open.
t144: Will there be an online mode at launch?
t145: Rockstar confirmed that, at launch, GTA VI is a single-player experience centered on Jason and Lucia. Plans for multiplayer have not been detailed yet.

n02: The Extended Look is out: 26 minutes of real GTA VI gameplay
n03: Rockstar finally showed the game running. It's 26 minutes captured on a base PlayStation 5 — not a dev machine — alternating between cinematics and pure gameplay with Jason and Lucia across Vice City and the state of Leonida. The presentation premiered on Netflix and arrives free on Rockstar's YouTube channel and the official site at 9 PM ET. It's the biggest look at the game in nearly three years of waiting.
n05: Red Dead 2-style NPC interaction — and yes, you can pet the dog
n06: Holding a trigger, the player picks from a few prompts to interact with anyone nearby, exactly like Red Dead Redemption 2. The demo opens with Jason and Lucia picking up a package in a run-down building, and the first thing the internet noticed was a dog being petted. Car theft changed too: you can use a slim jim to pop the door without smashing the window.
n08: The sixth wanted star is back
n09: Absent since GTA IV, the sixth wanted level reappears in the HUD. Rockstar didn't show what happens when the meter fills completely — but it did show far more chaotic police chases, and Port Gellhorn has its own police force, a sign that Leonida will have multiple jurisdictions.
n11: Instant switching between Jason and Lucia — and a karma system
n12: When the two are together, character switching is instantaneous: you can drive as one and hop to the other in the passenger seat with no transition. Apart, the switch takes a few seconds, like in GTA V. Jason also has a slow-motion ability that highlights lethal shot zones (red) and incapacitation zones (yellow) — the first hint of a morality system.
n14: Leonida is far denser than San Andreas
n15: The streets look visibly busier than GTA V's, and one scene shows Jason weaving through a packed nightclub with an NPC density new to the series. Among the activities glimpsed: street races, jet skis, scuba diving, basketball, dirt biking and even weightlifting. Clothing and accessories can be customized on the fly, through a wheel similar to the weapon selector.
n17: The Netflix premiere splits the community — and the leak ends in anticlimax
n18: Putting the premiere behind a subscription annoyed part of the fanbase, and Netflix error reports spiked minutes before showtime. Meanwhile, the supposed leak of the game's source code circulating this week turned out to be a 113 GB file full of zeros and a virus. At VICEVERSA we keep reporting the leaks without showing them.
m03: Stylized map of the state of Leonida with its six regions
m06: Six regions confirmed by Rockstar, estimated by the community at 1.5 to 2 times the size of GTA V's map. Hover, tap or navigate with Tab. Scroll to zoom and drag to pan.

m08: Original schematic illustration by VICEVERSA, drawn from the names, descriptions and relative positions officially released by Rockstar. Rockstar has NOT published an official map of Leonida — what circulates as one comes from a leaked build, which we neither use nor reproduce. The coastline is procedurally generated and proportions are approximate.
m12: The metropolis on the southeast shoreline and the heart of the state. Skyscrapers, art deco, beach and the highest crowd density in the game — the packed nightclub scene in the Extended Look came from here. It's where Jason and Lucia's story is centered.
m15: The swamps and mangroves covering southwest Leonida. Rivers, channels and isolated communities, with dangerous wildlife and boat crossings. This is the region that replaces the empty rural filler of previous games with something Rockstar promises is packed with things to find.
m18: The tropical archipelago to the south, linked by bridges and sea routes. It's where Jason comes from, having spent time working for local drug runners. Diving and jet skis both appeared in the Extended Look.
m21: The former west coast tourist town, now sustained by cheap motels, shuttered attractions, docks and truck stops. Rockstar portrays it without romance. It has its own police force, hinting at multiple jurisdictions across the state.
m24: The industrial town on the shores of Lake Leonida, the large body of water at the center of the map. Its economy revolves around the Allied Crystal sugar refinery, and the region is biker gang territory.
m27: The national park to the north, with real terrain, dense forest and wildlife. It's the closest Leonida gets to Red Dead 2's Ambarino: remote, scenic and built for off-road exploration.
m43: Vice City's international airport, north of the city. It's reported to be one of the fast-travel points between regions of the state.
m47: The working port that sustains Port Gellhorn: stacked containers, cranes running around the clock and active rail lines. Rockstar shows the contrast between legitimate commerce and whatever takes advantage of the blind spots.
m51: The sugar refinery that dominates Ambrosia's skyline. In Rockstar's own words, it provides the jobs — and the local biker gang provides almost everything else.
m55: The national park running along the state's northern border, with dense forest, canyons and rivers. Trails, rough terrain and dirt-road escapes.
m59: The strip of sand separated from the mainland by a bay, pure Miami Beach: art deco, boardwalk and the nightlife seen in the Extended Look.
m63: The apartment where Jason and Lucia begin the story, out in the southern islands. It's where the pair set off from into the rest of the state.
m67: The flooded heart of the Grassrivers, where airboats arrive as a vehicle class built for shallow water. Gators and dangerous wildlife off the main road.
